correctness.rationale: For each connected A subset of a tree, the event it is one exact open-edge component has probability p^{|A|-1}(1-p)^{|∂A|}; summing |A|/n over |A|>=3 proves the exact nF_T identity. Exhaustive nonisomorphic tree enumeration through n=6 (counts 1,1,2,3,6) and independent open-edge-state counting reproduced every six-vertex polynomial. Exact factorization gives 6(F_S6−F_D6)=p²(1-p)(2-p)(6−7p) and 6(F_T6−F_P6)=p²(1-p)(3−4p), with all other shapes strictly intermediate. First-order one-closed-edge expansion near p=1 gives F_T(1−q)=1−L(T)q/n+O(q²) at each fixed n; L(star)=n−1 versus L(double-star)=n−2; L(path)=6 versus L(two-two-arm tree)=n+1 for n>=6. This proves both infinitely extending extremality failures without misusing the n<=6 census.

value.rationale: There is a natural epidemiologically motivated three-person cluster-tail extremum that changes identity at sharply identifiable transmissibilities. The n=6 threshold and all-order one-closed-edge mechanism supply a motivated finite cutoff and explain why naive universal star/path heuristics fail; result applies to the precisely defined independent-bond proxy only.
